blueprint.objective: Transform a raw internal policy document into a validated, structured FAQ for employees, ensuring every extracted rule is represented and no rules are invented.

tasks.responsibility: Inspect the raw policy_text to confirm it is recognisably a policy document with identifiable sections (e.g., purpose, scope, definitions, rules, effective date). Record any structural problems (missing sections, ambiguous headings, incomplete clauses). Output a boolean is_valid flag, the list of detected section names, and a list of structural problems found.

tasks.role: Extract policy rules and defined terms
tasks.responsibility: Using the validated document structure (sections, is_valid, problems from validate_document) and the raw policy_text, extract every concrete, actionable rule and every defined term. Each rule must be traceable to a specific passage in the source. Do not infer or invent rules beyond what the text states. If is_valid is false, still attempt extraction but flag the risk in the output.

tasks.role: Reviewer for Extract policy rules and defined terms
tasks.responsibility: Review the output of 'Extract policy rules and defined terms' against the rubric.

output_schema.name: approved
output_schema.description: True only if every criterion is met

output_schema.name: feedback
output_schema.description: Concrete revision instructions for the maker

tasks.role: Write the employee FAQ in plain language
tasks.responsibility: Convert the extracted rules and definitions into a plain-language FAQ in Markdown. Produce exactly one question per rule. If an audience (reader group / reading level) is supplied, calibrate vocabulary and sentence complexity accordingly; if absent, default to a general-employee reading level. Include a short definitions section for any terms in the definitions list. Do not add legal advice. Output the full FAQ as Markdown and the count of questions generated.

tasks.role: Reviewer for Write the employee FAQ in plain language
tasks.responsibility: Review the output of 'Write the employee FAQ in plain language' against the rubric.

output_schema.name: approved
output_schema.description: True only if every criterion is met

output_schema.name: feedback
output_schema.description: Concrete revision instructions for the maker

patterns.rationale: these tasks consume predecessor outputs; run in dependency order

rubric: Every item in rules and definitions is directly traceable to a passage in policy_text; no rule is paraphrased into a new obligation not present in the source.
No concrete rule or defined term from the source is omitted.
Rules are stated as discrete, actionable statements rather than vague summaries.
No legal advice or interpretation beyond the document's own language is introduced.
question_count equals the number of items in the rules list from extract_rules (one question per rule, no more, no fewer).
Every rule from extract_rules is represented by at least one FAQ question; no rule is silently dropped.
No question or answer introduces content, obligations, or interpretations absent from the source rules and definitions.
No legal advice is present; the FAQ restates policy, not counsel.
Language complexity matches the audience parameter when provided, or a reasonable general-employee level when it is not.

missing_information: The PRD does not define what constitutes 'identifiable sections' for a policy document (e.g., a required set of headings such as Purpose, Scope, Definitions, Rules, Effective Date, Review Cycle). validate_document needs a concrete checklist or a permissive heuristic.

The PRD does not specify the Markdown structure of the FAQ (heading levels, whether to use a table of contents, whether definitions are a separate section or inline). write_faq needs a template or format spec.

The PRD does not state the behaviour when validate_document returns is_valid = false: should the pipeline halt, should extract_rules and write_faq still run with a warning, or should a fallback output be produced?
The PRD does not specify a maximum or minimum number of rules, nor how to handle very long or very short policy documents.
The PRD does not define what 'plain-language' means quantitatively (e.g., a target Flesch-Kincaid grade) when audience is omitted, making the default reading level ambiguous.
